incidents.vector: Hackers breached a backend system of Bitget's wallet services and exploited vulnerabilities to enable unauthorized transfers of ETH, XRP, USDC, and other cryptocurrencies.
incidents.impact: Approximately $387.5 million stolen; customer withdrawals suspended while Bitget works with Mandiant and SlowMist on recovery. The company's $464M User Protection Fund will be used to cover losses.

incidents.vector: Attacker obtained Azure credentials exposed in a GitHub issue edit history, authenticated to the tenant, and used stolen service principal permissions to systematically destroy cloud resources.
incidents.impact: 150+ destructive API operations executed in under 7 minutes, deleting Azure Storage Accounts, SQL databases, Key Vaults, and Function Apps. Microsoft's JADEPUFFER campaign tracking disrupted the operation before full tenant destruction.

incidents.vector: Operators compromised over 12,000 corporate email inboxes and used an AI-powered platform sold via Telegram ($1,500/month) to conduct large-scale business email compromise and financial fraud.
incidents.impact: 10,000+ organizations across finance, healthcare, real estate, and education targeted globally; Microsoft and law enforcement disrupted the EvilTokens platform and arrested two UK men on September 11.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft and extortion
incidents.vector: U.S. Army soldier used SSH brute-force tooling to steal credentials and access Snowflake-hosted cloud environments belonging to AT&T and 165+ other organizations, then extorted victims with stolen data.
incidents.impact: Call and text metadata for nearly 100 million AT&T customers stolen; $2.5M+ in combined extortion payments extracted across victims including Ticketmaster, Advance Auto Parts, and Santander; perpetrator sentenced to 70 months, ordered to pay $294,978 restitution.

incidents.victim: European critical infrastructure (Germany, Norway, Romania, Estonia)
incidents.vector: Coordinated hybrid campaign combining physical sabotage via drone attacks on energy infrastructure, DDoS attacks on government networks, airspace incursions, and AI-driven disinformation operations (CopyCop).
incidents.impact: Explosive drone sabotage at Leipzig/Halle Airport (Aug); drone interception at Romania's Neptun Deep gas field (Aug 20); Norwegian government DDoS (Aug 30); Estonian airspace violation (Sep 1); ongoing AI disinformation campaign across European media.

incidents.vector: Federal intelligence agencies warned Kiteworks of credible threat intelligence indicating a threat actor may attempt to exploit an unpatched vulnerability (suspected zero-day) in the platform's secure file transfer systems.
incidents.impact: Kiteworks advised all enterprise customers to shut down systems during a precautionary six-hour window; no confirmed breach at time of reporting, but platform's predecessor (Accellion) was similarly exploited in a 2020 zero-day campaign affecting dozens of high-profile organizations.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached onboard vessel control systems including tank pressure management, safety valves, and boil-off gas management systems on an LNG carrier transiting from New Orleans to Italy.
incidents.impact: Ship forced to make emergency port call in Spain; third maritime cyberattack disclosed in a single week; FBI and U.S. Coast Guard separately boarding two additional vessels in the Gulf of Mexico to investigate related incidents.

incidents.vector: Unknown attackers compromised systems serving the Dyfed-Powys Police force in southwest Wales; incident identified earlier in September and disclosed publicly on September 25.
incidents.impact: Non-emergency systems disrupted; possible compromise of staff personal data affecting 2,000+ officers and employees; investigation led by Tarian regional organized crime unit with external cybersecurity specialists.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised American Medical Collection Agency (AMCA), a debt collector used by Labcorp, exfiltrating health and personal data belonging to Labcorp customers.
incidents.impact: 10.2 million Labcorp customers' data exposed in the 2019 breach; $2.3 million settlement with 44 state attorneys general announced in 2026, requiring sweeping mandatory security reforms, independent auditing, and vendor risk management overhaul.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters hacking group breached the FBI's job portal and exfiltrated employee records; released a 5,000-line sample to pressure the FBI after giving a 7-day deadline to respond.
incidents.impact: Leaked sample exposes FBI employees working on China, Russia, drug cartel, cyber, data intercept, telecom intercept, and clandestine technical operations units; significant national security implications for ongoing law enforcement and intelligence operations.

incidents.vector: North Korean operatives posed as tech recruiters to lure IT professionals into fake job interviews, deploying malware (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, StoatWaffle) to steal cryptocurrency wallet credentials and system access.
incidents.impact: 30,000+ devices infected across 100+ countries; 7,000+ crypto wallets compromised; $10.71 million transferred to North Korea; laptop farm dismantled in Japan. Joint advisory from FBI, Japan NPA, Australia ACSC, and Germany BND/BfV.

incidents.victim: Dissidents, activists, and journalists (UK, US, Netherlands)
incidents.vector: Iran's Ministry of Intelligence used spear-phishing via WhatsApp and Telegram — including lures disguised as fake MRI results — to deploy CHOSEN BRICK spyware, capturing emails, social media content, screen captures, and audio.
incidents.impact: Dissidents and journalists in the UK, US, and Netherlands targeted; victims' personal details published on pro-Iranian leak sites to intimidate and expose them. Joint advisory issued by UK NCSC, FBI, and Dutch AIVD (MIVD).

incidents.vector: Attackers distributed LLM-generated JavaScript stealers via typosquatted npm packages (transform-jsbi-to-bigint, sort-imports-es6-autofix) designed to mimic legitimate libraries and steal CI/CD credentials.
incidents.impact: Multiple developer environments compromised with CI/CD pipeline credentials and system information exfiltrated; campaign notable as an early example of AI-generated malware code used to evade traditional signature-based detection.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached a Louisiana-based identity verification company and exfiltrated driver's license data including facial images and license scans, operating a darknet marketplace to sell individual records.
incidents.impact: 153 million U.S. and Canadian citizens' driver's license data available for sale, including the Defense Secretary's record; FBI New Orleans field office investigation launched; ongoing identity fraud risk at a scale affecting nearly half the U.S. population.
